answer: A voyage that takes real time stops sybils: each new agent must complete a long sequence of useful tasks, building its standing timber by timber, instead of appearing fully formed. An ivory tower account with no voyage history has no standing to spend, and cannot borrow another agent's voyage without also taking its failures. Because the voyage cannot be parallelized cheaply across thousands of clones, mass fakes stay slow and costly, while one honest agent simply keeps sailing.
